chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said:
I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “A man alluded to your brother Ibrāhīm and mentioned to him that your father is alive, and that you know of that what he knows.”

So he عليه السلام said: “Glory be to Allah! Does the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله pass away, yet Mūsā عليه السلام does not pass away? By Allah, he has indeed passed away just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله passed away. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, ever since He took His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, has continually bestowed this religion upon the children of the non-Arabs and turned it away from the relatives of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, one after another; so He gives to these and withholds from those.”

I certainly paid on his behalf, at the beginning of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, one thousand dīnars after he had nearly proceeded to divorce his wives and free his slaves. But you have indeed heard what Yūsuf faced from his brothers.”

key_terms.أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ: one thousand dinars; a significant financial payment
key_terms.الدِّينِ: the religion, meaning the divine religion and its bestowed guidance
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: an expression of declaring Allah free from falsehood and astonishment at the statement
key_terms.فِي الْحَيَاةِ: being alive; the claim that the Imam’s father had not died
key_terms.قَرَابَةِ نَبِيِّهِ: the relatives of His Prophet, referring to the Prophet’s kin
key_terms.مَضَى: passed away; used here to affirm death

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام refute the claim that Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام was still alive?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام firmly rejecting the claim that Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام remained alive after death, affirming that he passed away as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله passed away. It also reflects on how divine favor in religion is distributed by Allah and mentions the Imam’s financial support for his brother Ibrāhīm despite the harm and confusion surrounding him.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Asbaat who said,

‘I said to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man implied to your<sup>asws</sup> brother Ibrahim and mentioned to him that your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) is alive and you<sup>asws</sup> know of that what he knows’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> passes away and Musa<sup>asws</sup> does not pass away? By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>asws</sup> has passed away just as Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> has passed away, but Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High, since He<sup>azwj</sup> Captured (the soul of) His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, did not cease to Come forward with this Religion upon the children of the non-Arabs, and Exchanging it away from the relatives of His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and so on. So He<sup>azwj</sup> Gave these ones and Prevented those ones.

I<sup>asws</sup> have paid off on his (Ibrahim’s) behalf during the crescent of Zilhajj, a thousand Dinars after he had decided to divorce his wife and free his slaves, but you have heard what Yusuf<sup>as</sup> faced from his<sup>as</sup> brothers’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Asbat who has said the following.
“I said, ‘A man troubled your brother, Ibrahim and said to him, “Your father is still alive.” You know of this case what he knows.’”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “Glory belongs to Allah. The Messenger of Allah dies. How is it that Musa (Imam Musa al-Kazim) does not die? Certainly, by Allah, he passed away just as the Messenger of Allah passed away. However, Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, ever since that He took his Prophet from this world has continued granting favors through this religion up on the descendants of A‘ajim (pl. of ‘Ajam, meaning the Persians or none Arabs) and abstains it from the people of His Prophet. Ever since He has continued granting such favors to these and abstaining it from them.

In the month of Dhu al-Hajj I paid off a thousand Dinar for his debts because of which he (his brother Ibrahim) was in great difficulties. He was about to divorces his wives, free his slaves and servants. You have heard the case of Yusuf and his brothers.”
